doc.title: Joseph Rene and Edna Kelly Interview, 1969-12-15

chapter: Joe Rene: Lewis, the Rena band and New Orleans
title: First meeting George Lewis and where he bought his clarinet
summary: Rene retells hearing the flute at Governor Nicholls Street, persuading Lewis to buy a clarinet, and the Fink pawnshop on Rampart where it was bought.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: And I heard a flute playing, and I was wondering who, he was living in the back. See, right section, the other half of the house. And I stand up, I stand, I must have stand up there about 15 minutes, listen to that cover. I said, I'm going to go talk to this fellow. I didn't even know his name. I said, man, when he come in, oh, God, I said,
Mr. Rene, he said, oh yeah, come on in, Rene.

I got to talk, and I said, oh, you playing that flute? I said, you play that flute? Well, good. Then I began questioning him about making them shorts and them flats, you see. Right. Because the fellow didn't know how to make them kind of things on the flute can't do nothing, but he did, you see. Then he could blow his soul powerful, then he could force some different tones out of it. The boy could hear him play a fight. Him and Bé-Shane played the same way. I said, I told him, I said, look, I said, I think we might need a clan that's here. I said, I think you could make a good clan that's here. So, sure enough, went and found Ramport Street. And before I know he hadn't bought the clan there,
he went and bought the clan there. He got a beef-like clan there. Can you remember the name of where he bought it? Oh, let's see. You know, you weren't talking about it.

of Fink, it's the Eagle Loan office, not... It's the what? Eagle Loan office. Yes. His wife, but I think his wife doesn't matter. You see old man Fink, and that's who's his son's wife. She's there now, deals with her right now. And I think that's where he bought that plan, because mostly everybody, most all cut cutters, who they deal with Fink. He doesn't deal with nobody else. And most of his deal, just with Fink, he was living... He was on Ramport, he was driving and he was dealing. Right across the street from
that store where we played that number, yes. Oh, I see. That's right downtown. Huh?
That's right downtown. Yeah, see. Then after the name of the old lady, the Tick Tock.
